github.title: Dispatch a subagent item with worktree isolation and delete its branch at the close
github.author: jerridan

identity.head: 107678583a978d1a307a237d9273188089fb2c0e
identity.description:
Dispatch a subagent item with worktree isolation and delete its branch at the close

## Summary

A subagent item now gets its worktree from the dispatch, with `isolation: "worktree"`, and not from a `git worktree add` that the subagent runs. The guard of a worktree-isolated orchestrator session refused that command, and the subagent then built inside the orchestrator's own worktree. The close of a subagent item also deletes the branch of a merged PR now.

**Ticket:** N/A
**Type:** Bug fix

---

## Agent context

### Authority

`skills/orchestrator/references/subagent-items.md` owns the subagent item. `skills/orchestrator/references/resume-and-close.md` step 3 and `skills/orchestrator/references/launcher.md` "remove" own the removal flags and the proof rules. Design section 15.165.

### What changed, by file

- `skills/orchestrator/references/subagent-items.md`: "The dispatch" orders `isolation: "worktree"` for work that changes a repo, and says the orchestrator writes the returned path and branch into `subagent.worktree` and `subagent.branch`. "The record" writes both as `null` first. "The close" runs step 3 with its flags, and puts a notice in the inbox when the worktree is `null` and the branch is set.
- `docs/design.md`: finding 165.
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`: version 0.1.133.

### Constraints that applied

No second copy of a rule: the close points at step 3 of `resume-and-close.md`. The inbox notice is the smaller rule, so the close needs no branch-only delete path. A grep of `skills/`, `agents/`, `README.md` and `docs/design.md` found no other text that says the subagent adds its own worktree.

### How this was verified

Read the three sections against `resume-and-close.md` and `launcher.md`. Grepped for `worktree add` and "adds its worktree". No script runs this.

### Known gaps

No run has exercised it.


### Review findings fixed

The blocking finding and the early-record suggestion are fixed in their threads. Two findings outside the diff are fixed too: a new dispatch of a subagent that cannot resume gives no isolation and names the recorded worktree and branch (`subagent-items.md` "The dispatch", pointed at by `resume-and-close.md`), and the `worktree` and `branch` rows of `orchestrator-record.md` match the new rule.

triage.summary: Subagent items now get their worktree from the Agent tool's `isolation: "worktree"` dispatch. Before, the brief told the subagent to run `git worktree add`, and the isolated session's guard refused that. The orchestrator writes the worktree path and branch from the agent id right after the dispatch and checks them against the task notification. A re-dispatch names the recorded worktree and has no isolation. The close runs step 3 on that worktree and puts a notice in the inbox when a branch has no worktree. Items in another repo become implementer items. The change also bumps the plugin version and adds a design note.

findings.claim: The rule assumes the spawn result returns the agent id at once and that a task notification follows, but the dispatch mode it uses can be a foreground subagent dispatch, which returns only when the subagent finishes and sends no task notification.
findings.evidence:
The spawn result gives the agent id at once. Right after the
  dispatch, write `item <id> set subagent.worktree <checkout top
  level>/.claude/worktrees/agent-<agent id>`
findings.suggested_fix: Say the dispatch runs with `run_in_background` (or say how to get the worktree from the final tool result in foreground mode), and name the source of the agent id for each dispatch mode.
findings.explanation: In subagent mode without `run_in_background`, no id comes back until the work is done and no `<worktree>` notification arrives, so the record write and the check never happen as the rule says.

findings.claim: The path is built from the orchestrator's `<checkout top level>`. In a worktree-isolated orchestrator session, that is the orchestrator's own worktree, which may not be the root where the Agent tool puts isolation worktrees.
findings.suggested_fix: Get the path from `git worktree list --porcelain` by matching the branch `worktree-agent-<id>`, not from the top level of the current checkout.
findings.explanation: If the guessed path is wrong and the session restarts before the notification corrects it, the resume sees the `build` worktree as gone and the close runs `remove` on a path that does not exist.

findings.claim: A re-dispatch with no isolation tells the subagent to work in another worktree's path. In a worktree-isolated orchestrator session, the same guard that refused `git worktree add` may refuse edits or a `cd` outside the session's worktree.
findings.evidence:
A new dispatch of a subagent that cannot resume: give no `isolation`. The
  brief names `subagent.worktree` and `subagent.branch`, and says to work in
  that worktree on that branch
findings.explanation: The non-isolated subagent inherits the orchestrator's cwd and guard, so it may fall back to building in the orchestrator's worktree, which is the failure this change is meant to fix.

findings.claim: The close runs step 3 on `subagent.worktree` whenever it is set, but the Agent tool removes an isolation worktree on its own when the subagent made no changes. `remove` is then run on a path that no longer exists, and the branch is never cleaned up.
findings.evidence:
Run its
step 3 on `subagent.worktree` when it is set, with the flags of that step,
so the branch of a merged PR is deleted.
findings.suggested_fix: When `subagent.worktree` is set but gone and `subagent.branch` is set, handle it like the null-worktree case and put a notice in the inbox.
findings.explanation: A recorded worktree that is gone falls into neither case (set and present, or null with a branch set), so the branch can be left behind with no notice.

first.rationale: The dispatch mode follows the project-lead table, which requires `run_in_background: true` for a named dispatch in subagent mode, so the id and notification flow holds there. Only the first foreground dispatch and teammate mode are uncertain, and the finding does not show those apply to subagent items.

mode follows the table of `skills/project-lead/SKILL.md`'s "Every dispatch

1. Dispatch it without `run_in_background`, and alone.

In subagent mode, that first dispatch runs in the foreground and blocks

| `run_in_background` | never: a teammate does not support it | always, after the first dispatch |
escalated.rationale: The new text sends the dispatch mode to the project-lead table. That table makes the first dispatch of each session a foreground one in subagent mode, and the orchestrator has no other agent dispatches, so a subagent item can easily be that first dispatch. In that case nothing comes back until the subagent ends, and the rule's "agent id at once" and "task notification" steps do not hold. Later dispatches in subagent mode run in the background, so this is an edge case and not the normal path.

first.rationale: The worktree already exists as a sibling under the checkout's .claude/worktrees; the guard refused `git worktree add`, not edits in an existing worktree. The finding is speculative about the guard refusing edits or `cd`, and the file doesn't show that. The fallback also isn't the orchestrator's own worktree, since the brief names the recorded path.

The same design notes say the guard's behavior differs between Claude Code versions, so only a run can settle whether a re-dispatch with no isolation gets refused.

first.rationale: The Agent tool removes an isolation worktree, and its branch, only when the subagent made no changes. A merged PR means there were changes, so the worktree is kept and step 3 has a path to remove. An item with no changes has no branch left to clean up. The only open point is whether `remove` copes with a missing path, and that is an edge case.

write `item <id> set subagent.worktree <checkout top
  level>/.claude/worktrees/agent-<agent id>`
raise Fail(GIT, "launcher: the worktree %s does not exist" % path)
worktree, main_tree, gitdir = linked_worktree(path)
escalated.rationale: It is true that the record can keep a path the Agent tool has already removed. The harm the finding describes does not follow. `launcher.py remove` fails loudly when the worktree does not exist, so the orchestrator sees an error rather than a silent skip. And when the tool auto-cleans a worktree with no changes, its branch is removed with it and has no commits to keep, so nothing is left behind unnoticed.
